Wakeup, ownership transfer and error semantics of robust futex death handling.
Encoding and validation of native robust list next pointers and modifier bits.
Registration, unregistration and lifetime rules for the task robust list head.
Full field layout of task futex state, private hash control and bucket objects.
Hash function, bucket selection and global hash fallback behavior.
Meaning of futex key contents and hash bucket reference protection.
Priority inheritance waiter queueing, boosting and timeout behavior.
Scheduler wake queue mechanics and preemption control around deferred wake.
Architecture hook that extracts a pending robust operation from register state.

findings.text: Futex backed rt mutex release that acquires wait serialization, delegates the unblock decision, releases serialization, then performs deferred wakeups only when requested.
Per memory context futex setup that prepares private hash tracking alongside robust unlock range state.
Per memory context futex teardown that releases the per cpu reference counter, any staged replacement hash, and the currently published hash.
Automatic private hash sizing that derives bucket count from thread population and online processor count within global bounds.
Critical section range reset that clears stored ranges and then marks them unusable until reprogrammed.
Task exit and exec release orchestration that brackets central futex teardown with entry and exit protection.
Post exec reactivation that moves task futex state from terminal to healthy under pi serialization without exit serialization.
Fault fixup for robust unlock critical sections that clears a pending list operation inferred from register state when one is present.
Robust list teardown visits each queued lock once, suppresses double handling of an entry that is also pending, stops after a fixed bound, and yields cooperatively during long walks.
Compatibility robust handling separates a packed user word into an address portion and a modifier portion, then locates the futex by adding a stored table offset to the decoded base.
Native robust teardown resolves each futex from its list node plus a per task displacement and treats already queued locks differently from the lone pending addition handled after traversal.

Priority inheritance exit draining nests task serialization, bucket serialization, mutex wait serialization and task serialization again, validates continued ownership after reacquisition, detaches and disowns the state before unlocking, and performs the final mutex release outside.
Exit protection holds a per task mutex across teardown while the exiting marker is published and later cleared under pi serialization, forcing concurrent attachers to block and reevaluate.

Inner futex mutex release requires wait serialization on entry, empties ownership when idle, otherwise enqueues the next waiter for later wakeup and keeps preemption controlled until the deferred wake runs.
Task futex liveness moves from healthy to exiting under exit protection, then to dead when protection drops, with a recursive exit shortcut and a later return to healthy after successful exec.

Private hash reference tracking migrates from distributed counters to one shared counter through grace periods, using a large bias to avoid a transient zero, folding and clearing distributed values, then waking waiters if the folded result reaches zero.
Replacement hash choice prefers caller supplied over automatic, prefers disabling private hashing over keeping it, otherwise keeps the larger table and discards the smaller on races.

Private hash creation validates slot counts, publishes the reference counter exactly once under concurrency, keeps custom requests waiting until any staged pivot can proceed, and never reenables private hashing after it was disabled.

Default hash sizing scales with the smaller of thread count and processor count, rounds up, clamps to a fixed floor and the global ceiling, and does nothing when a custom table exists or the current table is already large enough.
Exit time user reads can fault; the observed behavior abandons the remainder of robust processing rather than retrying or reporting an error.

A waiter may release its inheritance state while exit teardown holds task serialization; teardown detects the lost reference acquisition, drops serialization to allow progress, then retries and rechecks linkage.
Flag marking a caller supplied private hash table rather than an automatically sized one.
Central task cleanup handles native robust locks, then compatibility robust locks when enabled, then inheritance states, clearing each source pointer once processed and skipping absent sources.
Unlock critical section ranges use an all ones start address as the invalid sentinel; duplication preserves programmed ranges while fresh contexts start invalidated.
Several facilities provide empty alternate definitions that perform no work when the corresponding configuration is unavailable.
Bucket setup initializes waiter accounting, an ordered wait chain, and bucket serialization for each newly allocated slot.
